models_evaluated: 34 LLMs (specific names not reported in text)

links.outcome: Cross-model robustness of correctness and consensus with vs without evidence-grounded agentic retrieval
links.effect: Agentic retrieval reduced inter-model decision dispersion (median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13) and increased robustness of correctness across models (mean 0.74 vs. 0.81); majority consensus increased (P<0.001).
links.quote: Agentic inference reduced inter-model decision dispersion (median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13) and increased robustness of correctness across models (mean 0.74 vs. 0.81).

links.outcome: Correctness and agreement across heterogeneous models on radiology questions
links.effect: High agreement did not guarantee correctness; consensus strength and robust correctness correlated (rho=0.88 zero-shot; 0.87 agentic).
links.quote: Consensus strength and robust correctness remained correlated under both strategies (\r{ho}=0.88 for zero-shot; \r{ho}=0.87 for agentic), although high agreement did not guarantee correctness.

links.outcome: Clinically assessed severity of incorrect LLM outputs
links.effect: Among 572 incorrect outputs, 72% were associated with moderate or high clinically assessed severity; inter-rater agreement was low (kappa=0.02).
links.quote: Among 572 incorrect outputs, 72% were associated with moderate or high clinically assessed severity, although inter-rater agreement was low (\k{appa}=0.02).

unlisted_practices: Evaluating cross-model consensus/entropy as a reliability measure for agentic pipelines
Analyzing response verbosity as a correlate of correctness

screen.reason: Evaluates 34 LLMs comparing zero-shot inference to agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning (a retrieval grounding safeguard) to measure impact on collective reliability and robustness across radiology QA.
